title_he: הוֹי שֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים הַנַּדִּיב, נִכְרַע לִפְנֵי גְדֻלָּתְךָ
review: The hymn is Hebrews 1:3 and Isaiah 53: 2:1–2 is Heb 1:3 (אֲשֶׁר הוּא זֹהַר כְּבוֹדוֹ וְצֶלֶם עַצְמוּתוֹ) almost word for word, 3:2–4 Isa 53:7 with 2 Cor 8:9, 4:2 the Gethsemane of Luke 22:44, and 5:2–3 Isa 53:6,11 with Rev 1:5.

1:1 שֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים — the Arabic يَا حَمَلَ اللهِ is John 1:29's ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ; the Hebrew uses the Gospel's own שֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים rather than כֶּבֶשׂ, because the title is fixed in the tradition and the line is an address.

2:2 וְצֶלֶם עַצְמוּתוֹ — the Arabic وَذَاتُ رَسْمِ شَخْصِهِ is the Greek ὑποστάσεως χαρακτήρ; עַצְמוּת is the noun behind the liturgical עֶצֶם, and the construct with צֶלֶם keeps the verse's claim that the Son is the exact impress, not a likeness.

3:3 בָּאֵבוּס — the Arabic الْمِذْوَد is the manger; אֵבוּס is the biblical feeding-trough (Isa 1:3, יָדַע שׁוֹר קֹנֵהוּ וַחֲמוֹר אֵבוּס בְּעָלָיו), and the verse is quoted because the stanza is moving from Bethlehem to the cross in one breath.

3:4 כַּגֵּר — the Arabic كَالْغَرِيب is 'as a stranger'; the Hebrew keeps גֵּר, the resident alien of the Torah, which carries more than 'stranger' — it names the One who had no inheritance in the land. 4:4 נִתְדַּלֵּיתָ is the printed reversal 'how poor You became, O Rich One' (2 Cor 8:9).
